# ParSEval: Plan-aware Test Database Generation for SQL Equivalence Evaluation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#parseval)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4750-miao.pdf) · PVLDB 18(11), 2025, pages 4750-4762

**Reading coverage:** All thirteen PDF pages, Sections 1-7, Definitions 1-6, symbolic/hybrid algorithms, coverage constraints, experimental tables and figure descriptions; no appendices.

## Research question

Fixed databases and local SQL mutations miss inequivalence caused by operator interactions, ties, multiplicity and grouping.

## Method

ParSEval expresses logical-plan operator behaviors as coverage constraints, then solves for small databases. A hybrid approach speculatively assigns concrete values to reduce symbolic expressions, with fallback solving. Relaxed coverage avoids enumerating every constraint combination.

## Evaluation

Four corpora include BIRD/Spider model predictions and human-written LeetCode/literature pairs. Comparisons use a 360-second timeout. Pair-aware evaluation generates tests from both queries; a separate experiment precomputes suites from gold queries alone.

## What the results support

The hybrid implementation improves supported-query coverage and counterexample discovery against the evaluated open-source baselines. A manual BIRD inequivalence audit reports 91.01% recall. Gold-only suites are smaller and faster than original databases but still admit 41 false positives in the reported experiment.

## Limits and qualifications

NULL multiplicities, special functions and unseen extra joins can evade generated tests. Supported/unknown outcomes and timeouts affect comparisons; some competing provers were excluded for missing released foreign-key support. Complete branch coverage is not a proof of unrestricted query equivalence or reference-intent validity.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Offers richer execution evidence and concrete counterexamples for evaluating SQL verifiers and candidate generation.
